questions.question: A smooth function has zero gradient at a point. What can we conclude?
options: It is stationary; curvature or other evidence is needed
questions.explanation: A zero gradient is compatible with a minimum, maximum or saddle. Even second-order information can be inconclusive in flat directions.
optionFeedback: Stationarity alone does not establish global optimality. Inspect curvature, nearby values and any convexity assumptions.
A zero gradient is compatible with a minimum, maximum or saddle. Even second-order information can be inconclusive in flat directions.
A valid stationary point can have a zero gradient. Check the derivative independently before blaming the optimizer.
